Systems methods practice 32

  • Systemic systems methods practice

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice

    Free exercises, worked examples, and answers for technical dry runs of systems methods.

  • Standards coverage and limits

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/coverage

    Editorial mapping to the public SCiO framework and apprenticeship standard, with explicit limits.

  • Checked practice resources

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/resources

    Free and paid learning routes, labelled by resource type, access, and review status.

  • Task sheets without answers

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/worksheets

    Printable tasks for an independent attempt or work with a practice partner.

  • Worked comparisons and answer keys

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/answers

    Worked steps and check questions, while preserving room for defensible alternatives.

  • Using the practice pack

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/tutor-notes

    Guidance for learners, tutors, and practice partners.

  • Systems concepts: make your boundary inspectable

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/systems-concepts

    Construct and challenge two systems-of-interest descriptions without confusing your model with the situation.

  • Systems laws: test variety, feedback and local optimisation

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/systems-laws

    Use a small disturbance-response model to test a claim about regulation.

  • Transposing theory: move up to a pattern and back down

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/transposing-theory

    Test a structural analogy rather than importing a solution because two situations sound alike.

  • Soft Systems Methodology: build a model that follows its purpose

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/soft-systems

    Move from a messy situation through purposeful perspectives to a logically defensible activity model and comparison.

  • System Dynamics: build, calculate and challenge a queue model

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/system-dynamics

    Distinguish causal-loop reasoning from an executable stock-flow model and verify a small model by hand.

  • Viable System Model: diagnose functions and channels

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/viable-system-model

    Choose a recursion, identify operational units, and test management functions without turning the VSM into an organisation chart.

  • Critical Systems Heuristics: inspect all twelve boundary categories

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/critical-systems-heuristics

    Build an is/ought boundary critique and show how a change in boundary alters a judgement.

  • Confrontation Analysis: separate positions, options and credibility

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/confrontation-analysis

    Build a small options table and identify what would make a joint commitment credible.

  • INFORMED Group Dynamics: investigate the distinctions behind a decision

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/informed-group-dynamics

    Elicit contrasting meanings, make a small reflective map, and revise an inference about another person's position.

  • Interactive Management: construct a small interpretive structural model

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/interactive-management

    Use a precise relation, a small adjacency matrix and transitive reasoning to structure a set of enabling conditions.

  • Interactive planning: design the service you would choose now

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/interactive-planning

    Distinguish an idealised design from a forecast, then work back to feasible changes and learning.

  • Mosaic transformation and bubble strategy: sequence changes you can sustain

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/mosaic-transformation

    Test a change sequence against available capacity, released capacity, dependencies and a protected experiment's interfaces.

  • Multi-methodology: justify the move from one method to another

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/multi-methodology

    Design a short inquiry in which each method answers a different question and its output is translated carefully into the next.

  • Patterns of Strategy: model dependence, fit and timing

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/patterns-of-strategy

    Analyse a strategic relationship and test a proposed move against relative dependence and response time.

  • Socio-Technical Systems: redesign the work and technology together

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/socio-technical-systems

    Find where variation is handled and design a jointly workable social and technical arrangement.

  • Syntegration: test the communication structure before the event

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/syntegration

    Understand overlapping participation and repeated cross-topic learning through a small structural rehearsal.

  • SODA: build a means-ends map without erasing disagreement

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/soda

    Turn supplied statements into contrasting constructs and a traceable means-ends map.

  • Fractal Enterprise Model: alternate processes and the assets they depend on

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/fractal-enterprise-model

    Build a small process-asset model and identify a neglected asset-management dependency.

  • Critical social learning: build a learning relationship across boundaries

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/critical-social-learning

    Design a small collective inquiry that can change both action and the assumptions behind it.

  • Service systems: follow demand and distinguish activity from resolution

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/service-systems

    Classify a small demand sample, trace end-to-end work, and design a prediction-led test.

  • Participative inquiry: test who your evidence leaves out

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/participative-inquiry

    Build an engagement and evidence plan that does not confuse influence with the right to be heard.

  • Futures and probes: test robustness without pretending to predict

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/futures-and-probes

    Compare options across explicit scenarios, then design more than one bounded learning probe.

  • Ethics and power: make an intervention's authority and effects explicit

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/ethics-and-power

    Distinguish permission, participation and legitimacy, then design a reversible intervention with an accessible challenge route.

  • Evaluation and reflexivity: test the claim you are tempted to make

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/evaluation-and-reflexivity

    Distinguish a measured change from a causal claim and use evaluation to revise both intervention and framing.

  • Systemic constellations: use a spatial representation as a hypothesis

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/systemic-constellations

    Explore a fictional organisational relationship with objects, then test what the representation does and does not establish.

  • Systemic conversations: expose inference and repair a broken commitment

    transduction.systems/systems-thinking/practice/systemic-conversations

    Separate data from inference and turn an ambiguous request into a discussable commitment.
